single_line_comment.comment: The hard recursion limit baked into TProtocol (_defaultRecursionDepth).
Build a CoRec/CoRec2 chain that is exactly [depth] structs deep.
Serialize via the generated write() over a fresh protocol of the given kind.
Deserialize via the generated read() over a fresh protocol of the given kind.
A chain one level below the limit must round-trip cleanly.
A chain exactly at the limit must still round-trip (off-by-one guard).
Writing a chain one level over the limit must be rejected.
Reading a too-deep payload must be rejected.
The same bound must apply to recursive exceptions.

Exercises the recursion-depth limit through the *generated* struct read/write path (TBase.write / TBase.read) -- the real code path that deeply nested input exercises -- rather than calling TProtocol.incrementRecursionDepth / decrementRecursionDepth in isolation.  The recursive IDL types come from test/Recursive.thrift, generated into the `Recursive` package: CoRec <-> CoRec2 form a mutually recursive chain and RecTree is a wide tree of nested structs.  Dart hard-codes the limit at TProtocol's _defaultRecursionDepth (64), so the boundary is: a chain of 64 structs round-trips, 65 is rejected with DEPTH_LIMIT.

Build a CoError/CoError2 exception chain that is exactly [depth] structs deep. Exceptions are read/written through the same generated path as structs, so the same bound applies. The chain terminates in a null field, which the generated write() skips, so [depth] structs nest exactly [depth] levels.

Craft a [depth]-deep nested-struct payload with raw protocol primitives, bypassing the recursion counter (which lives in the generated write()). This is the only way to obtain an over-limit payload, since a normal write() of such a chain would itself be rejected at the limit.
Craft a [depth]-deep nested CoError payload with raw protocol primitives. Uses the real recursive field (id 1, type STRUCT) so the reader recurses through the guarded generated read(), not skip().

Decrement regression guard: a wide (shallow) tree whose total number of struct-begins far exceeds the limit must still round-trip. This only holds if decrementRecursionDepth() unwinds each sibling back to depth 1.
A cyclic object graph would recurse forever without the limit; it must instead fail with DEPTH_LIMIT.
CoRec -> CoRec2 -> null close the loop: CoRec2.other -> CoRec
